Plongée dans les coulisses des grands dossiers d'actualité qui font débat à l'Assemblée nationale. Des enquêtes et des reportages pour donner du sens à l'actualité législative, politique, économique ou sociale.

After a notorious gangster is freed from prison, he seeks revenge for a betrayal that cost him his criminal empire and the life of his father.

A bookish library clerk working for a CIA front is hunted after he stumbles across a covert intelligence operation. Returning from lunch, he finds the entire office massacred. A true story of two remaining officers desperately trying to rally their meagre force of 105 men against 4,000 attacking Zulu warriors. Cetshwayo, ruler of the Zulu kingdom, begins his war against the white invaders with the annihilation of the British army at Isandlwana and moves on to his next target - the depleted garrison at Rorke's Drift.

Doctors worry that a mechanic could lose his crushed arm, and Dr Luke's decision not to ride a bike in the city is reinforced when he treats a cyclist who's been hit by a car.

Dr Andrew Trezise is worried that a young dirt bike rider has sustained life-altering injuries in a crash. And Dr Jonathan Papson fears for a show jumper who's in agony after being thrown off a horse.

Showing how A&E is somewhere that wisdom and insight is passed not just from medic to medic, but also from generation to generation. Fifteen-year-old Linden is brought in having badly cut his leg while back-flipping off a shed roof onto a trampoline.
It's a busy Mothering Sunday at King's as 23-year-old builder Jamie is rushed in by paramedics having fallen from the roof of a three-storey building, landing on a brick wall.
Married couple Mo and Anthony are looking for a holiday flat with sea views in Torremolinos on Spain's Costa del Sol. Laura Hamilton shows them five properties for their £130k budget.
George Clarke looks back at some of the most amazing houseboats people have built for the Great British waterways.
Sara Damergi helps recently engaged Michelle and Steve find the perfect family holiday home in and around the beautiful villages of Haute-Vienne in southern France, for their £100k budget.

Jasmine Harman jets off to the seaside town of Sitges in northern Spain to help Richard find his holiday home, with help from his best friend Peter. Jasmine shows Richard five properties for his budget of £210,000, are any of them the perfect one?

Leah Charles-King is in Spain's Mar Menor to help Eileen from Birmingham find the perfect holiday home. Eileen ideally wants a two-bedroom flat near the beach, and with a maximum budget of £43,500, Leah lines up five great options.

Shelley loves the Greek islands and has visited almost 30 of them. Laura Hamilton is tasked with finding Shelley and her partner Adrian's dream holiday home on the Greek island of Zante, for a budget of £75,000.

Ben Hillman helps Paula and Phil. With Phil close to retirement, they cannot wait to buy their very own holiday home by the sea around La Duquesa, on Spain's Costa del Sol. Ben shows them what their budget of £200,000 can buy.

Yvonne and Graham want a bolthole in the charming seaside town of Alvor on Portugal's Algarve. Ben Hillman attempts to find their perfect place, close to the harbour and the beach, and within their budget of £135k.

In north Surrey, planning enforcement officer Becky is joined by singing teacher Petrina, drum teacher Rob, solicitor Shoba and building company boss Giovanni. Becky plans to delight her guests with an evening of modern home cooking.

On the second night in north Surrey, Shoba is taking up the culinary gauntlet with an Indian menu, but the guests are less than impressed with Shoba's food. Is a bit of belly dancing, Bollywood-style, enough to save the day?
In north Surrey, 31-year-old drum tutor Rob is hoping his Thai-tastic menu will impress his guests, especially the object of his affections, Petrina.
In north Surrey, 49-year-old singing teacher Petrina is hoping her experiences entertaining on cruise ships will give her the edge, and is planning a showstopper of an evening.
The final night of the competition in north Surrey is hosted by Giovanni who wants to fly the flag for Sicily with some family-inspired recipes.
Jill hopes to charm her guests with her authentic 17th-century B&B, the Castle Arms Inn, in North Yorkshire. However, a rough night's sleep for two of her guests might scupper her chances.
The B&Bers are off to enjoy the great outdoors at Liz and Dave Johnson's Eden Valley glamping site in Cumbria, where the hosts show off their back-to-basics way of doing things.
At Fernie Castle in Fife, run by Neil and Mary Blackburn, there's plenty of traditional Scots splendour on show. However, two of the guests aren't impressed by the continental breakfast.
The last visit of the week is to the Cadillac Kustomz Hotel on the Isle of Bute, where owners Brody and Rima hope to rock their guests' worlds with a music-filled, retro retreat.
On payment day, there are certain complaints and breakfast blues as the B&Bers iron out their issues, before they find out how much they've been paid and who's won the week.

Paramedics and air ambulance medics treat a man who's collapsed and is in cardiac arrest. And a man who thinks the ache in his chest is just muscular gets a surprise when the paramedics tell him he's having a heart attack.
Matt treats a patient burnt in a workplace explosion, but bad weather jeopardises the flight to hospital.

In Hartlepool, the heli-medics are tasked with treating a man hit by a train. Cyclist Trevor suffers serious injuries after a collision with a car, and 12-year-old motocross biker Arai in Cumbria is flown across the country for emergency surgery.
After a brief courtship, Celeste and Jason get engaged. Celeste then asks her pastor father, who's not ready to let his daughter go, to officiate their Christmas wedding.

A serious TV newscaster's life changes when he meets his young superfan and the boy's hardworking single mum. As he embraces positive holiday stories, romance blooms - but a career opportunity forces him to choose between ambition and love.
Sparks fly between an emergency room doctor and a cardiologist as they work together to deliver three babies just in time for Christmas.
A New York City book editor takes on a temporary gig running a Maine bookshop for the month of December. While battling with the owners' son, she rediscovers her passion for nurturing creativity.
A journalist faces old fears when she returns to her hometown ice rink to cover a story. With the help of the owner and his young daughter, she begins to reevaluate her life's purpose.
An old audio cassette of her dad's voice sends a woman on a journey to retrace her family's most memorable moments at Christmastime.
Interior designer, Rose DeMonte, uses her skills back in her hometown to renovate a Christmas Charity Home for her brother Sal and his contractor Brysen's home flipping company.
When Emily wishes for a perfect Christmas like the ones found in the popular Sugarplum movies, she's shocked when Sugarplum herself appears to help her fulfil it.

A Naughty-or-Nice inspector evaluating a girl's Christmas status falls for her widowed father, making her question the strict rules of her consulting firm and forcing her to choose between protocol and love.
A woman and her roommate embark on a road trip to Yuletide Springs, a town where Christmas is celebrated year-round.
A couple hosting Christmas decide to fake their relationship after choosing to separate. However, working together for the holiday helps them remember why they fell in love.

Albert is neither the most attractive nor the most confident man in the world, so when he falls in love with one of his firm's clients, Allegra Cole, he calls in an expert to help him win her over. Hitch is the business name of Alex Hitchins, and he earns his pay by teaching men how to woo the girl of their choice.
After a bumpy ride, Leah and Ricci finally sort out their differences.
Charlotte calls an emergency meeting and makes a shocking announcement.

Sam hopes to fill the void of his late wife with new love Patricia. But Patricia's flirtation and demands for marriage without a prenup make Sam question if his boo has an ulterior motive; Tami steps in to uncover what, or who.
Singer Ashlee Simpson, wrestler Stone Cold Steve Austin and rapper Bizarre.
During the Palos Hills High School ski excursion for all the senior students, ongoing rivalries finally boil over into heated disputes.
We have a look at ordinary teenagers Ashlee and Anthony who live in extraordinary homes, and hear from the parents who give them whatever they want.
Catelynn copes with her decision to choose adoption at a retreat with other birth mums. Maci and Ryan reach out to a counsellor for help. Farrah wonders if she should stay home more with her baby.

There is excitement in the air as 600 hopefuls arrive for the preliminary auditions. Each contestant has less than two minutes to perform a freestyle dance routine in front of the judges. Only 115 dancers will reach the semi-finals, and only 75 will be called back to the final auditions for a chance to compete against the returning veterans.
A woman says her ex-neighbour assaulted her; he says she came after him with a bat.

A young woman claims she was swindled out of $7,500 of her college savings by her father's friend. He claims he needed $20,000 to start an online music business. A man claims the pedigree puppy he found in the middle of the road would have been euthanised if he hadn't taken him in. The pet's original owner is sued for his vet bills.
Brothers are accused of burglarising a neighbour's home, and former friends fight over a gun safe and a rifle scope.
A teen and his mother are accused of stealing a moped and stripping it for parts, and a woman sues her ex-lover for repayment of a loan.
A dog's owners sue the pet sitter for veterinary bills after the animal is hit by a car; a former friend sues a hair salon owner for repayment of loans.

A teen moves in with her older boyfriend and finds herself being sued for loans, rent, eviction fees and harassment. Plus, unable to find his campsite at a music festival, a man sues the teen with whom he was supposed to share the site.
A pregnant teen is sued for medical bills and property damage after she assaults another teen; a man sues former residents for leaving his duplex a mess.

A hit-and-run accident on the motorway and an alleged case of mistaken identity are disputed by feuding motorists. An allegedly stolen tax refund that was deposited into a two-year-old girl's bank account divides former friends.

A woman is suing her ex-fiancé for a loan to buy her engagement ring and down payments on a wedding reception and a home. He sues for the balance on her wedding dress. Child endangerment is the accusation laid against a nanny who sues her former employer for payment of her fee, lost wages and bank fees.
A woman's expensive lingerie goes missing; a man beats a pit bull after it attacks him.
The Avatars put their plan to transform the world into action, while Zankou kidnaps Brody and is forced to cast a paranoia spell on the Halliwell sisters.

As the sisters enjoy the peaceful new utopia, Leo realises that their conflict-free world comes at a terrible price they had not anticipated. He joins forces with Zankou to reverse the change and Brody is rewarded for his heroism.
Paige is hiring new professors for the Magic School and encounters a demon who has struck a deal with a sorcerer to become human.
A ghost possesses Darryl's friend, so Phoebe and Drake travel back to 1899 to the cabaret fire where the man was killed.
Piper is attacked by demons armed with thorns and ends up in a coma, but as she hovers between life and death, her spirit encounters a familiar face from the past.

Meeting online a year ago, Ayla felt an instant connection with Gabby, bonding over their shared sickle-cell struggles. However, with Gabby refusing to meet or video chat, Nev and Kamie feel that Gabby might not be the real soulmate.
Nev and Kamie smell a scam when Arturo's girlfriend, Laura, refuses to meet, video chat or talk on the phone after a year of dating.
Cristian fell hard for live streamer Chantel, but on her live, she never shows her face. With Chantel evading Cristian, Nev and Kamie come up with a clever plan to get them to meet.

Bella Swan is on the cusp of her 18th birthday and blissfully happy with her undead beau Edward Cullen. While celebrating her birthday with Edward's family of 'vegetarian' vampires, a frightening incident convinces Edward that he's simply too dangerous to be around his sweetheart. He decides to leave the town of Forks in order to ensure her safety - leaving her behind, angry and depressed.
Belieber Nathan decides it's time for Sketch to rid him of his embarrassing fan tatt. Alice clears things up for mixed-up Manga girl Kimberley, and Jay tackles a 'bad' tattoo of his idol.
A US navy warship is orbited by UFOs. Meanwhile, a British TV programme is interrupted by a voice claiming to be from the Ashtar Galactic Command, warning that Earth is in danger.

A UFO is caught on camera by a military helicopter on the Mexican border, an English woman is filmed disappearing from her bed at night, and NASA investigates UFOs after years of denial by the US authorities.

An eerie shape appears over Chicago. A man is fighting for his life after being shot by an unknown object, and a US military fighter jet appears to be being pursued by a UFO over the Bermuda Triangle.
A fleet of potential UFOs are filmed over the South China Sea, they seem to be appearing and disappearing, Plus, a 12,000-year-old archaeological site features carvings of extraterrestrial humanoids.

John Lennon and May Pang claimed to have seen a UFO from their balcony in New York, and a sinister visitor to a remote nuclear missile launch site in Montana, which more than 40 years ago caused nuclear missiles to be disabled for 24 hours.
A UFO is recorded flying straight from the sky into the sea with no loss of speed. Plus, astronaut Neil Armstrong goes in search of an ancient extraterrestrial library in the Ecuadorian jungle.
A mysterious opening on the Red Planet caught on camera, a UFO appears to invade an Amazon village, and an unidentified spacecraft disrupts the queen's jubilee celebrations in London in June 2022.
A man in Missouri films what looks like a metal cube spinning in the sky. Something very similar is seen in LA, Texas and Columbia.
Using drones and satellite imagery, discover a vanished Neolithic structure in an Irish field, an oasis in a Chinese desert and buried treasure in the UK.

Discover an array of mysterious phenomena seen from above, including a Nazi weapon in Northern France, a Russian military tower in the shadow of Chernobyl, and a forgotten Australian tunnel rumoured to hide a nuclear lab.
Discover over a hundred massive concrete arrows scattered across America, a mysterious hole in the middle of a lake in Southern California and more.
A Turkish drought reveals a long-lost Basilica and its secrets, while the hull of a ship in the North Sea answers decades-old questions.
Nubian pyramids reveal the rise of female power in Ancient Kush, while satellite images uncover secrets of an ancient Puebloan site in New Mexico.

Discover strange markings in the remote region of Northern Finland and reveal secrets found deep in the Antarctic. Drones find a Manhattan-sized mystery in a Vietnamese cave and a lost sky-high world in Mozambique gets a visit from above.
Drones reveal what's left of Henry Ford's American suburb in the Brazilian jungle, while clues to what killed a once-vibrant Pennsylvania mining town is discovered.
Look down over a constant inferno in Turkmenistan, mysterious circles in the Namibian desert and secret electric blue ponds in Utah.

Witness a remote island linked to one of the world's most famous aviation mysteries, explore thousands of shipwrecks in the Bermuda Triangle, and discover a 10,000-year-old mystery in the murky depths of the Yucatán Peninsula.
The Pyramids of Giza could be a map of the stars. First responders bring hope during Hurricane Katrina. And an Indonesian volcano erupts in a shade of blue.

Spaniens berühmte Costa del Sol erstrahlt plötzlich weiß. Schneit es mitten im Sommer, oder stecken Menschen dahinter? Können Satellitenaufnahmen endlich enthüllen, wie El Chapo, einer der berüchtigtsten Drogenbarone der Welt, aus Mexikos Hochsicherheitsgefängnis entkommen konnte? Außerdem entdecken Bildanalysten unzählige bunte Kreise in der Sahara. Kann es sich dabei um ein bisher unbekanntes Naturphänomen handeln? Die Doku forscht nach.

Auf den schottischen Inseln finden Forscher Hinweise auf sieben Ringe im Boden. In der Gegend lebten in der Vergangenheit viele kriegerische Stämme, deren Geschichte bis zu den Wikingern reicht. Aber als die Wissenschaftler dem Rätsel nachgehen, kommen sie zu einem vollkommen anderen Schluss. Außerdem entdecken die Satelliten eine zerstörte Stadt im Pazifik.
Die Sendung zeigt die größten Lkw-Unfälle und Kollisionen, die weltweit gefilmt wurden.

Diese Reise zeigt die erstaunliche Vielfalt der wilden Hunde. Vom arktischen Wolf über den geselligen Dhole bis zum kleinen Fennek und dem langbeinigen Mähnenwolf: Die Reihe entdeckt 37 faszinierende Arten und zeigt ihr Leben.

Der Flughafen in Bogotá gehört zu den wichtigsten Drehkreuzen Lateinamerikas. Jährlich sind dort 23 Millionen Passagiere und mehr als 500.000 Tonnen Transportgüter auf der Durchreise. Die Sicherheitsbeamten haben alle Hände voll zu tun.
Ein Satellitenbild aus dem Jahr 2005 zeigt möglicherweise eine prähistorische Kultstätte.

In England scheinen Satellitenbildern zufolge seltsame Gebäude zu stehen. Forscher sind neugierig. Als sie vor Ort sind, finden sie die Hinterlassenschaften einer furchtbaren Zeit. Auf Hawaii schockiert ein Fund eines steinigen Parallelogramms.

Berichtet wird über aktuelle Themen des Tages und die wichtigsten Entwicklungen in der Welt. Zudem werden Hintergründe und Einschätzungen von Politikern und Experten geliefert und es wird zusammengefasst, was die Menschen bewegt.

Abschied vom Handschalter! Wie das Selbstschalten sich langsam aus unseren Autos verabschiedet und warum dem Auto-Romantiker dabei das Herz bricht. Außerdem haben wir das interne Duell Dacia Duster gegen Dacia Bigster im Programm.

Zwischen staubigen Werkstätten und Weltklasse-Kunst: Ein Blick hinter die Fassaden der Alserkal Avenue enthüllt, wie ein emiratischer Geschäftsmann eine verfallene Marmorfabrik im Industriegebiet Al Quoz in Dubais führendes Kunstviertel verwandelte.

Beleuchtet werden Themen aus aller Welt und es Menschen und Geschichten hinter den Schlagzeilen aus der ganzen Welt gezeigt. Berichtet wird über beispielsweise über Atomversuche, Flüchtlinge und viele weitere Ereignisse rund um den Globus.
Die Sendung stellt diverse Reisen, Urlaubsziele, Länder und Städte im nahen und fernen Ausland vor.

Wolfram Kons auf der Kunstmesse Contemporary Istanbul. Wo einst osmanische Kriegsschiffe gebaut wurden, trifft heute die türkische Kunstszene auf internationale Stars. Hollywood am Goldenen Horn: Auch Johnny Depps Bunnyman ist dabei.

Das Magazin nimmt Themenfelder wie etwa Energiekosten oder Lebensmittelpreise unter die Lupe, die in Zukunft für den Alltag und somit für alle immer wichtiger werden. Darüber hinaus gibt das Magazin nützliche Tipps für das tägliche Leben.

Von den Aleuten in Alaska bis zu den Regenwäldern Panamas liegt die Pazifikküste Nordamerikas auf einer der aktivsten tektonischen Grenzen der Erde. Dort hat die Kontinentalverschiebung eine Vulkankette geschaffen, die sich über fast 10.000 Kilometer erstreckt. Diese Episode zeigt, wie diese Vulkane entstehen, wie sie wachsen und warum einige von ihnen Eruptionen auslösen, die stark genug sind, um Kontinente neu zu formen.

Europa liegt über einem brodelnden Flickenteppich tektonischer Aktivität. Unter den Städten, Wäldern und Küsten Europas liegen uralte vulkanische Narben, die sowohl seine Landschaften als auch seine Zivilisationen geprägt haben.

In Europa gibt es circa 100 aktive Vulkane, die auch jederzeit ausbrechen könnten. Innerhalb der Grenzen der EU sind es immer noch 30 Vulkane. Experten haben bescheinigt, dass sie potenziell gefährlich sind. Ein Ausbruch wäre eine große Katastrophe.

Die Themen sind "24/7 - der Supermarkt der niemals schläft", "Das vergessene Luxushotel", "Das aufwendigste Croissant der Welt", "In trockenen Tüchern - Handtuchproduktion", "So entsteht der schärfste Senf" und "Letzter Flug - Flugzeug-Recycling".

Drei ähnliche Todesfälle bringen die Ermittler 1994 auf die Spur des 23-jährigen Steve Grieveson. Doch er hat nicht nur drei Teenager ermordet und dann die Leichen in Brand gesteckt, sondern auch ein Fall aus 1990 geht auf sein Konto.

Im englischen Cumbria tötete der Taxifahrer Derrick Bird im Jahr 2010 bei einem Amoklauf insgesamt zwölf Menschen, elf weitere wurden dabei schwer verletzt. Als er von der Polizei umstellt wurde und seine Lage aussichtslos war, erschoss er sich.

Der Serienkiller Joachim Kroll ist als "Menschenfresser von Duisburg" bekannt. Als er 1976 endlich gefasst wird, findet die Polizei sein letztes Opfer: eine 4-Jährige, die er zerlegt hatte und im Kühlschrank und in einem Kochtopf aufbewahrte.

Ed Gein, der Schlächter von Plainfield, erinnert an Horrorfilme wie "Psycho". Als die Polizei nach einer vermissten Frau sucht, findet sie auf Geins Farm ein Horrorkabinett aus Leichenteilen, das er über zwölf Jahre zusammengestellt hatte.

Der Serienkiller Fritz Honka war über viele Jahre aktiv und misshandelte und ermordete Prostituierte. Nur zufällig wurde er gefasst, als Feuerwehrleute den Verwesungsgeruch bemerkten und dann die zerstückelten Leichen mehrerer Frauen fanden.

Militärhubschrauber sind unverzichtbar für die Bundeswehr. Sie dienen vielfältigen Zwecken wie Transport, Kampf und Rettung bei Land-, See- und Lufteinsätzen. Ihre Zuverlässigkeit und Schnelligkeit sind unter allen Bedingungen entscheidend.

Jeden Tag begegnen sich NATO und Russland in der Ostsee. Sechs Monate war die deutsche Fregatte Mecklenburg-Vorpommern hier im Einsatz. Für die Besatzung bedeutet das: Leben auf See, Arbeiten auf See - und im Ernstfall Kämpfen auf See.

Der Kollaps des Surfside "Condos" in Florida kostete fast 100 Menschen das Leben. Aber was sind die Gründe für die Katastrophe? Auch der Verlust des U-Boots "Kursk" und das Feuer an der Kings-Cross-Station in London werden untersucht.

Drei reale Katastrophen werden mit forensischer Präzision rekonstruiert. Darunter das Zugunglück von Lac-Mégantic, die Explosion in einer Zuckerfabrik in Georgia und außerdem die Havarie der "Ever Given" im Suezkanal im Jahr 2021.

Die F-22 Raptor ist besonders wendig, schnell, kann umfangreich bewaffnet werden und weist hervorragende Tarnkappeneigenschaften vor. Dank einer speziellen Beschichtung ist der Raubvogel für Radarsysteme nahezu unsichtbar.

Aus einem Treffen wurde das Manöver NATO Tiger Meet zu einer komplexen Übung mit internationaler Dimension. Im Mittelpunkt stehen deutsche Crews des Taktischen Luftwaffengeschwaders 51 Immelmann, die in Portugal anspruchsvolle Missionen fliegen.

Es wird die Produktion des Kettenfahrzeugs Lynx in Unterlüß und Ungarn begleitet. Ausgestattet mit dem Lance-Turm und modernster Hightech, erkennt er feindliche Angriffe und reagiert mit automatischer Zielverfolgung.

Am 24. März 2015 befindet sich die Maschine des Germanwings-Flugs 9525 auf dem Weg von Barcelona nach Düsseldorf. Urplötzlich verliert der Airbus A320-211 über den Alpen innerhalb kürzester Zeit an Höhe. Sofort leitet die französische Flugsicherung Notfallmaßnahmen ein und versucht, den Piloten zu erreichen. Vergeblich: Der Jet verschwindet vom Radar. Erst Stunden später werden in einer unzugänglichen Bergregion Wrackteile und die Überreste von 150 Menschen entdeckt.

Über der sturmgepeitschten Nordsee wird eine Turboprop-Maschine vom Blitz getroffen. Im Cockpit fallen die Instrumente aus, das Flugzeug rast in die Tiefe, der Aufprall scheint unausweichlich. Bei der Untersuchung wird etwas Ungewöhnliches entdeckt.

Bei einem Großeinsatz auf der Juarez-Lincoln Bridge werden zwei Frauen vorläufig festgenommen. Die Beamten überprüfen ihre Fracht auf illegale Schmugglerware. Auch der Lieferwagen eines älteren Mannes wird gründlich untersucht.

Auf der Gateway International Bridge suchen die Beamten nach einem Jugendlichen, der von zwei Kidnappern in einem Van entführt wurde. Auf der Juarez-Lincoln Bridge in einem Jeep finden die Beamten jede Menge verstecktes Bargeld.

Die Beamten rüsten sich für einen Großeinsatz: Ein Gefangener soll den mexikanischen Behörden übergeben werden, doch alle weiteren Einzelheiten unterliegen strengster Geheimhaltung, denn der Mann wird von einem brutalen Drogenkartell gesucht.

Es wird über eine große Auktion von Pkw-Oldtimern in Dallas, Texas berichtet, bei der an vier Tagen rund 1.000 Pkw versteigert werden. Der Autohändler Dieter Thiel aus Wuppertal hat sich auf US-amerikanische Oldtimer spezialisiert.

Der Ford Mustang ist ein unbestrittener amerikanischer Klassiker. Mit seinem Acht-Zylinder-Motor steht er nach wie vor für Kraft und Freiheit. Auch sechzig Jahre nach ihrem Erscheinen ist die Nachfrage nach gut erhaltenen Exemplaren hoch.
Gezeigt werden Geschichten über Luxusautos, Manufakturen und die Automobilgeschichte.

Es wird ein Blick hinter die Kulissen der größten Waschstraße der Welt in Stuttgart geworfen. Bis zu 4.000 Autowäschen und rund tausend Innenreinigungen nimmt der Familienbetrieb an einem Tag vor. Dafür ist ein enormer logistischer Aufwand nötig.

Spezial-Fahrzeuge, die das Dreißigfache ihres Eigengewichts bewegen können, werden vorgestellt. Ganz gleich ob Militärfahrzeuge geborgen werden sollen, Flugzeuge oder Raketen bewegt werden sollen: Sie sind optimal auf ihr Einsatzgebiet angepasst.

Die Arbeit als Hochseefischer ist trotz moderner Schiffe extrem gefährlich. Stürme, harte körperliche Belastung, unbeständiges Wetter und unsichere Fischpreise führen zu einem ständigen Wettlauf gegen die Naturgewalten und die Zeit.

Wir werfen einen Blick auf die Seenotretter der DGzRS, die bei Sturm und hohen Wellen auf Nord- und Ostsee im Einsatz sind. Begleitet wird die Crew eines Seenotkreuzers an der Elbmündung, die einen Eindruck von der Arbeit der Helfer vermittelt.

In der ehemaligen Tschechoslowakei rettet Oskar Schindler 1.200 jüdische Frauen und Männer auf einem Fabrikgelände vor dem Holocaust – die Geschichte und der Ort hinter "Schindlers Liste". Ein Ökohotel im Amazonas scheitert am Reality-TV, in Brandenburg bringt ein Kalkwerk Aufschwung mit fatalen Folgen für Arbeiter.

Diese Folge befasst sich mit einer Region des Nahen Ostens, die von Ruinen übersät ist. Außerdem wird in Taiwan ein seltsames Bauwerk erforscht, das die Herzen derjenigen, die seinen wahren Zweck kannten, in Angst und Schrecken versetzte.

Diese Folge wirft einen Blick auf einige unheimliche Ruinen, die in den bewaldeten Hügeln von Arkansas versteckt sind. Außerdem gibt es einen Blick auf ein heruntergekommenes Arbeitslager in Albanien, in dem Staatsfeinde untergebracht waren.

Diese Folge der Sendung wirft einen Blick auf eine Vulkaninsel vor der Küste Taiwans mit gruseligen Ruinen aus einer dunklen Ära. Außerdem wird eine Miniatureisenbahn, die in den Wäldern von Arkansas versteckt ist, erforscht.

Diese Folge der Sendung wirft einen Blick auf das Hartwood Hospital in Lanarkshire, Schottland. Das Gebäude war einst eines der größten psychiatrischen Krankenhäuser in Europa. Experten diskutieren über die dunkle Geschichte des imposanten Gebäudes.

Die Dokumentation zeigt die im Wald gelegenen höhlenartigen Kuppelbauten in Indien, die seit ihrer Darstellung durch die Beatles als "Ashram" berühmt geworden sind. Die heute bröckelnden Bauten waren einst der Gipfel des spirituellen Luxus.

Sie begegneten einander nie und blieben doch dauerhaft aufeinander fixiert: Hitler und Stalin. Sie stiegen auf zu Führern von Diktaturen, die an blutiger Gewalt alles übertrafen, was menschlicher Wille zur Macht bis dahin an Grausamkeit hervorgebracht hatte. Scheinbar gesichertes Wissen liefert neue Einsichten in alte Fragestellungen: Wie werden Menschen zu Diktatoren.

At the playground, Pedro and Penny's glasses fall off; both think that their glasses are broken, as they cannot see very well; Madame Gazelle shows Pedro and Penny different types of objects with lenses.
It's a snowy day and Peppa's family build an igloo for their snowman. They hide in it during a snowstorm, but Penny Polar Bear and her parents love snowstorms and also Peppa's igloo.

Peppa and her friends are at playgroup when they learn that Mr. Bull and Mrs. Cow are getting married the next day; everyone goes into a panic when they confess how they have done nothing to prepare for the big day.

Everyone prepares for Mr. Bull and Mrs. Cow's wedding; Peppa and the soon-to-be-weds go to the jewellers to get rings, to the dressmakers, to get a wedding dress and finally to Peppa's house to sort the wedding cake.
Holly spends the day with King Thistle on his royal duties. King Thistle must launch an elf boat, judge a fairy fruit competition and make a speech at the festival.
The children are at the Elf Farm, but to learn where milk comes from they must visit a big farm, to find cows. The children travel to Lucy Big's farm, where she shows them all the animals.
Peppa's family are at Digger World, where they have fun building walls and knocking them over again, and even help Mr Bull when there's an obstacle in the road.
Teddy needs mending and cleaning after rolling down hills and jumping in muddy puddles, so Peppa takes her to Miss Rabbit's Doll Hospital.

Mummy Pig is determined that George's new hat doesn't get muddy when Peppa and George visit Grandpa and Granny Pig. Everyone tries to make sure that it stays clean, even if it means that they get messy instead.
Mummy Dog surprises Captain Daddy Dog with a gift of a boat trip for his birthday, but when Peppa and the gang come along, the trip doesn't go to plan.
Madame Gazelle and Mr Bull lead the children to the wildflower wood to learn all about flowers; the children enjoy identifying the flowers like Wild Garlic, Bluebells and even a rare orchid.
Peppa and George play in their grandparents' garden on a very hot day, but they don't have a paddling pool; Granny and Grandpa Pig create their own water squeezers and even a water slide.

Daddy Pig receives a jumping stick in the mail and demonstrates to Peppa and George how to use it. Peppa and her friends struggle with using it first.
Miss Rabbit gives Peppa and her friends a tennis lesson, but the tennis balls get everywhere. Mr Stallion and Miss Corgi arrive with strawberries and cream.
Peppa and her family are on a caravan adventure; the first stop is the biggest potato in the world; when it starts to get too foggy, they park up for a rest before another busy day.
Bruno the brakeman learns the importance of teamwork and friendship when the engines help him complete his tasks during an unexpected windstorm.
Paddington builds a robot that he calls Paddington that requires a real friend to work, Baaz invites everyone to celebrate Diwali with him, and Paddington is his helpful assistant.

Paddington has a race against time in order to enjoy his first ever solar eclipse. Paddington accepts an inventor's award for Simi when she's too shy to step up, but it makes Simi feel jealous and sad.

The Browns meet Shantee the lighthouse keeper when they arrive at the beach for their holiday. Paddington, Jonathan, and Judy become trainee lifeguards and end up rescuing Mr Brown with Taylor the lifeguard's help.

Something is making the strange noises in the cave. Jonathan thinks it's a mermaid, but Paddington isn't so sure. Judy wants to find a fossil on the beach, but everyone else seems to be getting lucky except her. Paddington tries to help.
Peppa and her friends, accompanied by Mummy Sheep and Granny Sheep, take Vanessa to Grampy Rabbit's boatyard for inspiration. The children create various artworks using items found around the yard.
While Mummy and Daddy Pig attend a refresher antenatal class, Peppa and George join Miss Rabbit's Sibling School where they learn about what to expect when their new sibling arrives.
Peppa eagerly awaits her new sibling, growing impatient with the lengthy wait. Suddenly, Mummy Pig announces that the baby is coming right now.
The Pig family go to the hospital, where Peppa is determined to find the perfect name for the baby.
The nurse visits and decides to focus on teaching proper baby-holding techniques. She demonstrates a safe method for a small person, like Peppa, to hold an infant correctly.
George undergoes a medical examination to assess his hearing. The results of the test reveal moderate hearing loss in his left ear, marking an important milestone in his health and development.
Peppa is excited to help George explore the world of sounds now he has his hearing aid. She shows him her favourite sounds including the splashing of jumping in a muddy puddle!
Grandpa Pig and Grandad Dog are on their boats when Grandpa Pig drops an anchor on his foot! After an x-ray and plaster cast at the hospital, Grandpa Pig needs to stay overnight.

Daddy Pig receives a letter saying he must go away on business to test some very important concrete. Peppa, Mummy and George all decide to go with Daddy and enjoy a train journey, where they sing to pass the time.
